CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is the main purpose of engineering graphics?
options: To communicate technical design information accurately
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Engineering graphics communicates shape, size, construction, and other technical details through drawings.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which instrument is commonly used to draw circles and arcs?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A compass is used to draw circles and circular arcs.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is the purpose of a drawing scale?
options: To represent an object proportionally at a chosen size
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A scale relates drawing dimensions to actual object dimensions.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which line type is commonly used for visible outlines in technical drawings?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Visible outlines are conventionally drawn with continuous thick lines.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which line type is commonly used for hidden edges?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Hidden edges are conventionally represented by dashed lines.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is the usual purpose of a centre line?
options: To indicate axes or centres of circles and symmetry
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Centre lines indicate centres, axes, or symmetry in technical drawings.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What does dimensioning communicate?
options: The name of the drawing instrument
The sizes and locations of features
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Dimensions specify sizes, distances, diameters, radii, and locations.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which view is obtained by looking directly at the front of an object?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: The front view is the orthographic view projected from the front direction.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which view shows the object as seen from above?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: The top view represents the object as viewed from above.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is orthographic projection?
options: Representing an object with views projected perpendicular to projection planes
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Orthographic projection uses perpendicular projectors to create standard views.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is an isometric drawing intended to show?
options: A three-dimensional representation with the principal axes equally foreshortened
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Isometric drawings show three dimensions in one pictorial view using isometric axes.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: In an isometric drawing, what is the angle between the two receding axes on the page typically?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: The three isometric axes are separated by 120 degrees in space; the two receding axes are commonly drawn at 30 degrees to the horizontal.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which instrument is used to draw straight horizontal lines on a drawing board?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A T-square or parallel straightedge helps draw horizontal lines.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is the purpose of a set square?
options: To draw standard angles and perpendicular lines
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Set squares are used for perpendicular and standard-angle construction.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What does a sectional view help reveal?
options: Internal features that may be unclear in external views
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Sectional views expose internal geometry by imagining the object cut by a plane.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: A point located above the horizontal plane (HP) appears where in front view?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A point above HP is represented above the XY reference line in the front view.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: A point located in front of the vertical plane (VP) appears where in top view?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: In the usual first-angle convention, a point in front of VP has its top view below XY.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is the XY line in orthographic projection?
options: The reference line representing the intersection of HP and VP
The longest edge of every object
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: XY represents the intersection of the horizontal and vertical reference planes.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is the true length of a line segment?
options: Its shortest projected length in every view
The width of the drawing sheet
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: True length is the actual spatial length of the segment.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: When is a line parallel to HP shown in true length in its top view?
options: Only if it is vertical to HP
When viewed in a suitable orthographic projection, its top view is parallel to and represents its true length
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A line parallel to a projection plane appears in true length on that plane.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is a plane figure?
options: A two-dimensional shape lying in a plane
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A plane figure has length and breadth but no thickness in the geometric model.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which of these is a polyhedron?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A cube is a polyhedron bounded by polygonal plane faces.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: How many faces does a cube have?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A cube has six square faces.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: How many vertices does a cube have?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A cube has eight vertices.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: How many edges does a cube have?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A cube has twelve edges.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which solid has a circular base and one apex?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A cone has a circular base and a single apex.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which solid has two parallel circular bases and a curved lateral surface?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A cylinder has two parallel congruent circular bases.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is a prism generally characterized by?
options: One circular base and one apex
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A prism has two parallel, congruent polygonal bases connected by parallelogram faces.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is a pyramid generally characterized by?
options: A polygonal base and triangular faces meeting at an apex
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A pyramid has one polygonal base and triangular lateral faces that meet at an apex.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is a cutting plane in a sectional drawing?
options: A physical saw in every case
An imaginary plane used to cut through a solid to reveal its interior
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: The cutting plane is an imaginary plane used to define the section.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is the section of a solid?
options: The shape formed where the cutting plane intersects the solid
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: The section is the cross-sectional shape created by the cutting plane.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What do section lines or hatching usually indicate?
options: Material cut by the section plane
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Hatching identifies surfaces cut by the imaginary section plane.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is development of a surface?
options: Unfolding a surface onto a plane
Measuring an angle with a protractor
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A development lays out a solid's surface flat without stretching it, in ideal geometric construction.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which method is commonly used to develop the lateral surface of a cylinder?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A cylinder is commonly developed by the parallel-line method.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which method is commonly used to develop the lateral surface of a cone?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A cone's lateral surface is developed using a sector based on its slant height.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What does a transition piece connect?
options: A title block to a border
Two openings or sections of different shapes or sizes
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Transition pieces connect ducts or components with differing cross-sections.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is an isometric axis?
options: One of the three principal axes represented equally in an isometric view
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: The three principal axes in an isometric projection have equal angular spacing.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is the difference between isometric projection and isometric drawing?
options: Isometric projection uses foreshortened lengths; isometric drawing commonly uses true lengths along isometric axes
Isometric projection is a sectional view
There is no difference in any standard
Isometric drawing shows only one face
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Isometric projection applies isometric scale; an isometric drawing often uses true lengths for convenience.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which shape represents a circle in an isometric view on an isometric plane?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A circle on an isometric plane appears as an ellipse in the pictorial view.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What does CAD stand for?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: CAD means Computer-Aided Design.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is a major benefit of CAD?
options: Precise editing, drafting, and reuse of drawing data
It removes the need to check dimensions
It guarantees a design is safe
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: CAD improves drafting efficiency and precision, but drawings still require review.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: In CAD, what is a layer commonly used for?

Changing the physical material of an object
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Layers organize geometry such as dimensions, centre lines, and object outlines.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is a CAD block commonly used for?
options: Converting every line into a circle
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Blocks allow repeated symbols or components to be inserted and reused.

To change the object's physical size automatically
To make every line the same thickness
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Correct units and plotting scale help ensure drawing dimensions are interpreted correctly.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is a title block used for?
options: Recording drawing identification and key administrative details
Filling the entire drawing with colour
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: A title block commonly includes the drawing title, number, scale, date, and drafter information.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Why are standard symbols and line conventions used?

To make technical drawings consistent and easier to interpret
To make each drawing intentionally different
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Standards reduce ambiguity and improve communication between people using drawings.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is a dimension extension line used for?

Indicating the points or limits between which a dimension applies
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Extension lines extend from the feature being dimensioned to the dimension line.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is a scale of 1:1?

The drawing length is twice the actual length
The actual object is half the drawing length

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which projection view commonly shows the width and depth of an object?

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which projection view commonly shows height and width?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: The front view commonly shows height and width.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: What is a projector in orthographic drawing?

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Projectors carry point positions from the object to projection planes and between views.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which solid has one curved surface and no vertices?

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: A triangular prism has how many rectangular lateral faces?

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which method is commonly used for developing a prism's lateral faces?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Prisms are commonly developed using the parallel-line method.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which method is commonly used for developing a pyramid?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Pyramids are commonly developed by the radial-line method using true slant edges.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which CAD operation creates a duplicate of selected geometry at a new location?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Copy duplicates selected drawing objects.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which CAD operation removes the unwanted portion of an object using cutting boundaries?
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Trim removes portions of objects based on selected cutting edges or boundaries.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Zoom changes the view magnification, not the actual geometry.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Select the most appropriate option: What is a projector in orthographic drawing? Choose one option.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Select the most appropriate option: Which method is commonly used for developing a pyramid? Use standard engineering drawing conventions.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: For Class XII Engineering Graphics, identify the correct answer: Which CAD operation removes the unwanted portion of an object using cutting boundaries? Select the best answer.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Which statement best describes the concept? Which CAD operation changes the viewing magnification without changing the geometry? Use standard engineering drawing conventions.
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Zoom changes the view magnification, not the actual geometry.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: For Class XII Engineering Graphics, identify the correct answer: What is the main purpose of engineering graphics? Choose one option.
options: To communicate technical design information accurately
CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.why: Engineering graphics communicates shape, size, construction, and other technical details through drawings.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Choose the correct answer: Which instrument is commonly used to draw circles and arcs?

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: Choose the correct answer: Which line type is commonly used for visible outlines in technical drawings? Use standard engineering drawing conventions.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: For Class XII Engineering Graphics, identify the correct answer: What is the usual purpose of a centre line? Choose one option.

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: For Class XII Engineering Graphics, identify the correct answer: What does dimensioning communicate?

The name of the drawing instrument

CBSE 12 - Engineering Graphics.q: For Class XII Engineering Graphics, identify the correct answer: What is an isometric drawing intended to show? Choose one option.

To make each drawing intentionally different
